  "text": "Tobias waited until the church clock struck nine before he took the beach road. He had not slept. There was a button missing from his coat, and all through the service his thumb had worked the place where it had been.

From the gate he could see that Maren's door was shut.

He called her name. Then he called it as he had when they were children, before either of them had a house to answer from.

The latch lifted easily.

Her front room was in order. The lamp stood unlit on the sill. Her father's rug lay square with the boards. Tobias stayed in the passage, holding his cap by its brim.

There was nothing to tell anyone.

He went into the kitchen. A cup stood upside down beside the sink. He turned it over, then put it back the way it had been. He had come prepared to do something useful, and this was all he could find.

Outside, the eleven posts cast short shadows toward the house. He counted them on his way to the gate, touching each one. At the last he stopped to pick a splinter from his palm.

That evening he returned with a button sewn crookedly onto his coat.

He did not knock. He set a loaf beneath the porch bench, where the rain would not reach it.

Before leaving, he looked through the front window.

The lamp was still unlit.

He shifted sideways to see past his own reflection, but the room stayed empty.",
